assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative quantitative account of the long-run evolution of income and wealth inequality, with major consequences for research and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman are central and complementary contributors to the empirical measurement, interpretation and extension of this research programme.
assessment.maturity: The underlying evidence, datasets and subsequent research agenda have accumulated over many years.
uncertainties: The relative weight to place on broad empirical measurement versus causal mechanisms remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and organizational change provided a durable alternative framework for understanding innovation, firms and economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is unmistakably a foundational figure, though the formulation developed through a wider intellectual collaboration not fully represented in this candidate entry.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has had several decades to shape research in organizational, innovation and growth economics.
uncertainties: The candidate description necessarily compresses a broader intellectual lineage and attribution question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed modern trade theory and empirical analysis of the distributional and aggregate effects of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's framework is pivotal, while Helpman and Redding made major connected theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and extensively used in research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across a large related literature, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reshaped understanding of how trade and technological change alter local labour markets, tasks and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock and labour-demand components of the contribution.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been extensively examined and remain central to debates on adjustment to structural change.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of trade, technology and other local shocks remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The use of linked population administrative data made intergenerational mobility measurable at fine geographic and institutional scales and changed the empirical study of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are core contributors to the administrative-data mobility programme.
assessment.maturity: A substantial body of follow-on work has tested, extended and applied the approach.
uncertainties: Observed mobility patterns do not by themselves establish the causal mechanisms behind them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of exhaustible resources, natural capital and biodiversity into economic reasoning addresses a fundamental long-run constraint on prosperity.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal made foundational contributions to the economics of resources and intergenerational welfare.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have had a long scholarly life and have gained increasing relevance in environmental accounting and policy.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and inclusive wealth entails difficult conceptual and measurement choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their long-run assembly and comparative analysis of crises, debt and default made historical macro-financial regularities unusually accessible and influential.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are the clearly identified architects of this joint research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped scholarship and policy discussion through multiple financial episodes.
uncertainties: Some empirical claims and data handling associated with the programme have received important criticism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The systematic measurement of management practices established organizational capability as an important explanation of productivity differences across firms and countries.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are central originators, with Sadun a leading contributor to the connected empirical programme.
assessment.maturity: The research has generated replication, extension and practical influence across a broad set of economies.
uncertainties: Identification of the causal effects of measured management practices remains challenging in some settings.
